sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which part of the foot is best to use for a short, controlled pass to a teammate?
options: C) The inside of the foot
questions.answer: C) The inside of the foot

questions.question_text: In the traditional Indian game of Kho-Kho, what word must a player shout to tag a sitting teammate to run?
When holding a bat or racket to strike a ball, where should your eyes be focused?
options: B) On the ball coming towards you
questions.answer: B) On the ball coming towards you

questions.question_text: What is the physical movement called when you spring into the air on one foot and land on that same foot?
How should you position your hands to catch a ball that is thrown above your waist level?
options: A) Pinkies together, fingers pointing down
B) Thumbs together, making a 'W' or diamond shape
D) One hand behind your back
questions.answer: B) Thumbs together, making a 'W' or diamond shape

questions.question_text: In Yoga, Tadasana is also known as which pose?
options: B) Mountain Pose (or Palm Tree Pose)
questions.answer: B) Mountain Pose (or Palm Tree Pose)

questions.question_text: Why is it important to drink water (stay hydrated) during physical education class?
options: A) It makes you run slower
B) It cools the body and replaces fluids lost through sweat
C) It helps you kick harder
D) It makes the ball softer
questions.answer: B) It cools the body and replaces fluids lost through sweat

questions.question_text: What equipment is needed to play the traditional game of Pitthou (Lagori)?
options: A) A bat and a hard ball
B) A football and a net
C) A soft ball and a pile of flat stones
questions.answer: C) A soft ball and a pile of flat stones

questions.question_text: What should you do to stop a slowly rolling football with your foot?
options: A) Kick it as hard as you can
C) Gently place the sole (bottom) of your foot on top of the ball
D) Pick it up with your hands
questions.answer: C) Gently place the sole (bottom) of your foot on top of the ball

questions.question_text: Taking slow, deep breaths after a running game helps to:
options: B) Calm the mind and slow down the heart rate
questions.answer: B) Calm the mind and slow down the heart rate

questions.question_text: Describe the correct hand position and body posture to catch a ball that is rolling fast on the ground. (Answer in 1-2 sentences)
questions.answer: To catch a rolling ball, bend your knees to get low to the ground. Keep your pinky fingers together with your palms facing the ball to create a scoop.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain one way a player gets 'Out' in the game of Kabaddi. (Answer in 1-2 sentences)
questions.answer: A raider gets 'Out' in Kabaddi if they are tackled by the defenders and cannot touch the midline before running out of breath, or if they stop chanting the word 'Kabaddi'.

questions.question_text: Name two important activities you should do to 'warm up' your body before playing a fast running game. (Answer in 1-2 sentences)
questions.answer: Before playing, you should jog lightly to increase your heart rate and do simple dynamic stretches for your arms and legs to prevent muscle injuries.

questions.question_text: How do you position your body and legs when performing Vrikshasana (Tree Pose)? (Answer in 1-2 sentences)
questions.answer: To perform Vrikshasana, stand tall on one leg, place the sole of the other foot flat against your inner thigh, and join your hands together above your head while balancing.

questions.question_text: What is the correct body stance for hitting a ball with a cricket bat? (Answer in 1-2 sentences)
questions.answer: Stand sideways facing the bowler with your knees slightly bent. Keep your eyes on the ball, hold the bat firmly with both hands, and swing smoothly through the line of the ball.

sections.section_name: Section C - Sports Mechanics & Fill in the Blanks

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with the correct physical education terms:
1. Running is different from walking because in running, there is a moment where both feet are off the ___.
2. In Kabaddi, the player who goes into the opponent's half to tag them is called the ___.
3. When throwing a ball with your right hand, you should step forward with your ___ foot.
4. Practicing Tadasana regularly helps improve body ___ and tallness.
5. Doing a proper ___ before sports prevents muscle injuries.

Match the physical movement on the left to its correct Skill Category on the right:
1. Skipping forward
2. Catching a tennis ball
3. Sitting quietly and breathing deeply
4. Balancing on one foot
5. Striking a ball with a bat

Options:
a) Mindfulness / Yoga
b) Manipulative Skill
c) Locomotor Skill
d) Non-locomotor / Stability Skill
e) Manipulative Skill
questions.answer:
1. Skipping forward - c) Locomotor Skill
2. Catching a tennis ball - b) Manipulative Skill
3. Sitting quietly and breathing deeply - a) Mindfulness / Yoga
4. Balancing on one foot - d) Non-locomotor / Stability Skill
5. Striking a ball with a bat - e) Manipulative Skill

questions.question_text: During a game of Pitthou (Lagori), your team is losing. Your best friend gets very angry, kicks the ball over the fence, and refuses to play anymore. As a good teammate, what should you do and say to resolve this situation using good sportsmanship?
questions.answer: I would stay calm and not yell back. I would gently tell my friend, 'It is okay to lose sometimes, games are about having fun and playing together, not just winning.' I would ask them to take a deep breath, help retrieve the ball, and apologize to the other team so we can finish the game happily.

questions.question_text: Your P.E. teacher has asked you to plan a 5-minute 'cool-down' and mindfulness routine for your class after a very tiring and sweaty football match. List 3 specific steps you will make the class follow to calm their bodies and minds.
questions.answer: Step 1: Have everyone do a slow, relaxed walk in a large circle for 1 minute to slowly bring down their heart rate. Step 2: Have everyone sit down on the grass, stretch their legs forward, and gently reach for their toes to relax the leg muscles. Step 3: Ask everyone to close their eyes, place their hands on their knees, and take 10 slow, deep breaths in through the nose and out through the mouth to calm the mind.
